page: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the ESv3 family, configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores running at 2.6 GHz. This server features a hyperthreaded architecture with 2.0 threads per core and is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. A defining characteristic of this instance is its high memory density, providing 432.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 27.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 885 GB, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is weak, as evidenced by bottom-25% results in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks all falling into the middle 50% category. Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block reads and writes, consistently register average performance.

The primary tradeoff of the E64-16s_v3 is the disparity between its massive memory allocation and its modest single-threaded processing capabilities. While it offers high resource density for memory-bound tasks, compute-heavy workloads may experience bottlenecks due to the weaker single-core performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server is structured to optimize memory-per-resource ratios, making it a viable option for workloads requiring large datasets in memory without needing top-tier CPU speeds.

Given these characteristics, the E64-16s_v3 is suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, and caching systems. This is supported by average scores in Redis SET operations and Passmark database operations. It is also appropriate for static web serving and software compilation, but is less suited for heavy single-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference.
